```{r datawrangling, echo=FALSE}
# dataset loading and data wrangling

Project_data = read_csv("Project_data.xls", show_col_types = FALSE)

Project_data = Project_data %>%
  mutate(Nat_Home = factor(ifelse(tolower(Nationality) == "velorian", 1, 0))) %>%
  mutate(Total_F = ifelse(Total < 6, "low", ifelse(Total > 12, "high", "medium"))) %>% # creation of categorical variable: adjust thresholds if needed
  mutate(Total_F = factor(Total_F, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("low", "medium", "high")), # formatting
         across(c(Profession,Sex,MaritalStatus,WorkIncapacity,AlcoholCurrent,AlcoholAbuseCurrent,Cannabis,PathAcuteSub,PathChronic,young), ~as.factor(.x)),
         D_aggregate = ifelse(is.na(D_aggregate), "Other", D_aggregate),
         CGI=factor(CGI, ordered=TRUE, levels=as.character(1:7))) %>%
  mutate(CGI.na = factor(ifelse(is.na(CGI), 1, 0))) %>%
  filter(!(Municipality %in% c("GALVEN CROSS","FENNOCK","HALDRIM"))) %>% # remove individuals outside Valdoria and/or fow which no spatial data was available 
  filter(!(D_aggregate %in% c("Other", "Eating disorders", "Non-epileptic paroxysmal episodes"))) # remove those classes with less than 10 entries in D_aggregate; 8 observations lost
```

```{r NAtable}
tab_missing_values <- function(Project_data_3, filename_prefix = "missing_values_part") {
  missing_values <- colSums(is.na(Project_data_3))

  perc_missing <- (missing_values / nrow(Project_data_3)) * 100

  tab <- data.frame(
    Missing_Values = missing_values,
    Perc_Missing = round(perc_missing,3)
  )
  tab <- tab[order(-tab$Perc_Missing), ]

  # split in two parts for readibility
  n <- nrow(tab)
  midpoint <- ceiling(n / 2)
  tab1 <- tab[1:midpoint, ]
  tab2 <- tab[(midpoint + 1):n, ]
  
  export_tab <- function(subtab, filename) {
    kbl_tab <- kable(subtab, format = "html") %>%
      kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
    kbl_tab %>% as_image(file = filename)
    print(paste("Exported table:", filename))
  }

  export_tab(tab1, paste0(filename_prefix, "1.png"))
  export_tab(tab2, paste0(filename_prefix, "2.png"))
}

tab_missing_values(Project_data_3)
```

## Train/test split (before any imputation)

```{r split}
item_vars = grep("^(HAB|NET|RES|ACT)_", names(Project_data_02), value = TRUE)

Project_data_02 = Project_data_02 %>%
  mutate(outcome_obs = complete.cases(pick(all_of(item_vars))),
         Total_raw = rowSums(across(all_of(item_vars), ~as.numeric(as.character(.x)))),
         Total_F_raw = factor(ifelse(Total_raw < 6, "low", ifelse(Total_raw > 12, "high", "medium")),
                              levels = c("low", "medium", "high")))

set.seed(42)
obs_rows = Project_data_02 %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number()) %>%
  filter(outcome_obs) %>%
  dplyr::select(row_id, Total_F_raw)
split.obs = initial_split(obs_rows, prop = .8, strata = Total_F_raw)

Project_data_02 = Project_data_02 %>%
  mutate(is_test = row_number() %in% testing(split.obs)$row_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Total_raw, -Total_F_raw)

table(outcome_observed = Project_data_02$outcome_obs, test = Project_data_02$is_test)
```

## NAs in HAB, NET, RES, ACT.

Two-steps procedure:

- step 1: we first choose predictors for the questions of the different sections. If these variables have very few NAs, we fill them with the mode; otherwise we impute them using all other variables as predictors.
- step 2: we apply the MICE algorithm to fill the NAs in HAB_, NET_, RES_, ACT_ scores using a LASSO logistic regression model for binary variables (random forests where LASSO proved unstable), to impute the missing data based on regressors selected a priori.


```{r}
Modes = function(x) { # there is no built-in function for the mode, so we made our own
  ux = unique(x[!is.na(x)]) 
  tab = tabulate(match(x,ux))
  ux[tab == max(tab)]
}


Project_data_02= Project_data_02 %>%
  mutate(across(c(Profession, Children, Siblings, MaritalStatus), ~coalesce(.x, Modes(.x[!is_test])[1]))) # for some variables, we can use the mode to fill NAs


VAR_dataset <- Project_data_02 %>%
  dplyr::select(IllnessDuration, CivilDisability, Education, AlcoholCurrent, AlcoholAbuseCurrent,
                Cannabis, AlcoholPast, Substances) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Education, AlcoholPast, Substances, AlcoholCurrent, AlcoholAbuseCurrent, Cannabis), ~as.factor(.x)))

png("missing_patternVAR.png", width = 500, height = 500)
md.pattern(VAR_dataset, rotate.names=TRUE) # bottom line: n. of NAs for a certain variable; on the left we find the n. of lines with the represented configuration of NAs
dev.off()

methods <- mice::make.method(VAR_dataset)
# methods depending on variable type:
## numeric → pmm (predictive mean matching)
## binary → logreg
## multilevel factor → polyreg
## ordinal → polr
methods["CivilDisability"] <- "pmm"
methods["Education"] <- "polyreg"
methods["AlcoholCurrent"] <- "logreg"
methods["AlcoholAbuseCurrent"] <- "logreg"
methods["Cannabis"] <- "polyreg"
methods["AlcoholPast"] <- "logreg"
methods["Substances"] <- "polyreg"
methods["IllnessDuration"] <- "pmm" 

set.seed(42)
impVAR = mice(VAR_dataset, ignore = Project_data_02$is_test, m = 5, maxit = 50, method=methods, print = FALSE) # NA filling

png("plotVAR.png", width = 500, height = 800)
plot(impVAR, layout = c(2, 8),  cex.axis = 10, cex.main = 10, cex.lab = 10) # as the procedure is Markov-chain based, these graphs must be random and without trends
dev.off()

png("stripplotVAR_1.png", width = 700, height = 300)
stripplot(impVAR, CivilDisability+ IllnessDuration ~.imp, pch = c(1, 1), col = c("grey", "red"), cex = c(5, 5), hor=FALSE)
dev.off()

png("stripplotVAR_2.png", width = 700, height = 600)
stripplot(impVAR, AlcoholPast + AlcoholCurrent + AlcoholAbuseCurrent ~.imp, factor=0.5, pch = c(1, 1), col = c("grey", "red"), cex = c(4, 4), hor=TRUE)
dev.off()

png("stripplotVAR_3.png", width = 700, height = 600)
stripplot(impVAR,  Cannabis + Substances + Education ~.imp, pch = c(1, 1), factor=0.8, col = c("grey", "red"), cex = c(3, 3), hor=TRUE)
dev.off()

comp.VAR = mice::complete(impVAR, 1)

Project_data_02 = Project_data_02 %>%
  mutate(across(c(IllnessDuration, CivilDisability, Education, AlcoholCurrent, AlcoholAbuseCurrent,
                Cannabis, AlcoholPast, Substances), ~comp.VAR[[cur_column()]]))
```

```{r}
comp.HAB  = mice::complete(impHAB, 1)

  mutate(across(starts_with("HAB_"), ~comp.HAB[[cur_column()]]),
         across(starts_with("RES_"), ~comp.RES[[cur_column()]]),

  mutate(across(c(ID, Service, psychiatric, Education, Profession, MaritalStatus, AlcoholPast, AlcoholCurrent, AlcoholAbuseCurrent, Cannabis,

         across(c(IllnessDuration, CivilDisability, Children, Siblings), ~as.numeric(.x))) # fix the formats

Dataset.complete$CGI = as.numeric(levels(Dataset.complete$CGI))[Dataset.complete$CGI]
```

## Addition of summary variables for the different groups of answers Total, and Total_F (ordered factor)

```{r}
Dataset.temp = Dataset.complete %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with(c("HAB_", "NET_", "RES_", "ACT_")), ~ as.numeric(as.character(.)))) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(starts_with(c("HAB_", "NET_", "RES_", "ACT_"))), na.rm = FALSE))

Dataset.complete = Dataset.complete %>%
  mutate(Total = Dataset.temp$Total) %>%
  mutate(Total_F = ifelse(Total < 6, "low", ifelse(Total > 12, "high", "medium"))) %>%
  mutate(Total_F = factor(Total_F, ordered=TRUE, levels=c("low", "medium", "high")))

Dataset.complete %>%
  group_by(Total_F) %>%
  summarise(count = n())

sapply(Dataset.complete %>% dplyr::select(starts_with(c("HAB_", "NET_", "RES_", "ACT_")), Total, Total_F), class) # class check
```

## Territorial variables

```{r territory}
area_vars = c("Density", "Income_percapita", "Services", "Employment", "Culture",
              "Perc.online.purchases", "Download", "GreenAreas_perc")

var_groups = list(
  territory = area_vars,
  clinical = c("D_aggregate", "IllnessDuration", "CGI", "psychiatric", "CivilDisability"),
  substances = c("AlcoholCurrent", "AlcoholAbuseCurrent", "Cannabis", "Substances"),
  socio_demo = c("Sex", "Age", "Education", "Profession", "MaritalStatus", "Children", "Siblings"))

setdiff(names(Dataset.forest)[-1], unlist(var_groups))

Dataset.model %>%
  count(Municipality, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(perc = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))

Dataset.model %>%
  group_by(Municipality) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(area_vars), n_distinct)) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(area_vars), max))

area_lookup = Dataset.model %>%
  dplyr::select(Municipality, all_of(area_vars)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(Municipality = as.character(Municipality))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(area_lookup$Municipality),
          !anyDuplicated(area_lookup[area_vars]))

smotenc_municipality = function(df, outcome = "Total_F", k = 5, over_ratio = .8) {
  df %>%
    left_join(area_lookup, by = area_vars) %>%
    mutate(Municipality = factor(Municipality)) %>%
    dplyr::select(-all_of(area_vars)) %>%
    smotenc(var = outcome, k = k, over_ratio = over_ratio) %>%
    mutate(Municipality = as.character(Municipality)) %>%
    left_join(area_lookup, by = "Municipality") %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(names(df)))
}

smote_caret = list(
  name = "SMOTE-NC with municipality as nominal variable",
  func = function(x, y) {
    df = smotenc_municipality(bind_cols(tibble(Total_F = y), as_tibble(x)))
    list(x = as.data.frame(dplyr::select(df, -Total_F)), y = df$Total_F)
  },
  first = TRUE)

area_lookup %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(area_vars)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") %>%
  round(2)

icc.model = lme4::lmer(Total ~ 1 + (1 | Municipality), data = Dataset.model %>% filter(!is_test))
vc = as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(icc.model))
round(vc$vcov[1] / sum(vc$vcov), 3)
```

## Automatic selection - H2O AutoML

```{r, eval=FALSE}
h2o_start()
set.seed(42)
# same training and testing datasets used for the other models
total_train = train.forest
total_test = test.forest

# run for a maximum of 120 seconds
auto_char <-
  auto_ml() %>%
  set_engine("h2o", max_runtime_secs = 120, seed = 42, 
             save_data = TRUE,
             nfolds = 5,
             keep_cross_validation_predictions = TRUE
             )%>%
  set_mode("regression") # we consider the Total score as a continuous variable

recipe <- recipe(Total~., 
              data = total_train) 
auto_wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_model(auto_char) %>%
  add_recipe(recipe)

# AUC (area Under Curve) is excellent to check the ability of a model to separate different classes; for unbalanced dataset, it is better to use precision-recall AUC
# accuracy: the percentage of correct guesses of the model. Simple and direct, for balanced datasets only.
# logloss (Logarithmic Loss): wrong predictions are penalised depending on the assigned probability of the correct class (higher penalties if the correct class probability is low)
# Mean Per Class Accuracy separates information per class: helpful to locate "problematic" classes
```

## Total: single tree, manually parameters set

```{r}
set.seed(42)
test.fit = rpart(Total ~ .,
                 data = train.forest,
                 method = "anova", # for continuous variables
#                 parms = list(split = "gini"), # not needed for ANOVA
                 control = rpart.control(xval = 10, minbucket = 3, minsplit = 9, cp = 0,
                                         maxdepth = 5)) # 10 cross validation; cp = 0 for no pruning; at least 3 observations in every final leaf

print(test.fit) # `*` marks terminal nodes
printcp(test.fit) # re.error = proportion of errors in each node; xerror and xstd = error and st.dev of cross validation
test.fit$variable.importance # hierarchy of variables

rpart.plot(test.fit,
           type = 4)

# rpart.predict(test.fit, nn = TRUE, rules = FALSE) # posterior classification of individuals

cpt = test.fit$cptable
best.row = which.min(cpt[, "xerror"])
cp.1se = cpt[which(cpt[, "xerror"] <= cpt[best.row, "xerror"] + cpt[best.row, "xstd"])[1], "CP"]
test.prune.002 = rpart::prune(test.fit, cp = cp.1se) # As a rule of thumb, it’s best to prune a decision tree using the cp of smallest tree that is within one standard deviation of the tree with the smallest xerror.

print(test.prune.002)
test.prune.002$variable.importance
printcp(test.prune.002)

png("DecisionTreeTotal.png", width=1200, height = 700)
rpart.plot(test.prune.002,
           type = 4,
           cex=1.2,
           box.palette = "Oranges")
dev.off()

# rmse
pred_tree_test = predict(test.prune.002, newdata = test.forest)
round(sqrt(mean((test.forest$Total - pred_tree_test)^2)),2)
```

## Random forest (variables random sampling)

```{r}
# sometimes, some features are super important and will always be used --> trees will end up very similar, and this reduces the advantage of having more trees
# randomly subset some of the Xs at each split of each tree (one third of the total n. of Xs, the default for regression) --> RANDOM FOREST APPROACH
set.seed(42)
rf.complete = randomForest(Total ~ .,
                          data = train.forest,
                          mtry = max(floor((ncol(train.forest)-1)/3), 1),
                          importance = TRUE,
                          ntree = 1000)

png("Total_OOB_error_rf_mpred.png", width = 800, height = 500)
plot(rf.complete$mse, main = "OOB error - rf", xlab = "n. of trees", type = "l")
dev.off()

which.min(rf.complete$mse) #find number of trees that produce lowest OOB MSE
sqrt(rf.complete$mse[which.min(rf.complete$mse)])  #find OOB RMSE of best model
```

```{r}
                            data = dplyr::select(train.forest, -Total),
                           y = train.forest$Total,
                     label = "Random Forest")

plot(model_performance(explainer = explainer))
plot(model_diagnostics(explainer = explainer))
explainer.test = DALEX::explain(model = rf.complete,
                                data = dplyr::select(test.forest, -Total),
                                y = test.forest$Total,
                                label = "Random Forest")

plot(model_parts(explainer = explainer.test,
            N = NULL)) # feature importance; use all observations
plot(model_parts(explainer = explainer.test,
            N = NULL,
            variable_groups = var_groups))

# SHAP values

shap_perm = predict_parts(explainer, new_observation = instance,
                          type = "shap", B = 10)

test.forest$Total[7]
```

## Total: grid search

```{r cache = TRUE}
# 1. type of model definition
tree_char <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),  # cp
  tree_depth = tune(),       # maxdepth
  min_n = tune()             # minsplit
  ) %>%
  set_engine("rpart", model = TRUE) %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

mlp_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(tree_char)
mlp_param

# 2. model formula
recipe <- recipe(Total~., 
              data = train.forest)

# 3. tuning options
ctrl <- control_grid(verbose = FALSE, save_pred = TRUE)


# 4. workflow creation
wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(tree_char) %>%
  add_recipe(recipe)

# 5. hyperparameters grid to test
cost_complexity_values <- seq(0.01, 0.10, by = 0.01)
min_n_values <- seq(2, 7, by = 1)              
tree_depth_values <- seq(3, 10, by = 1)  

grid <- expand.grid(
  cost_complexity = cost_complexity_values,
  min_n = min_n_values,
  tree_depth = tree_depth_values
)

# 6. resampling with cross-validation (5-fold)
set.seed(42)
folds <- vfold_cv(train.forest, v = 5)

# 7. Grid search
set.seed(42)
res <- wf %>%
  tune_grid(
    resamples = folds, # resampling with cross validation.
    grid = grid, # grid to test
    metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae), # metrics to use for performances evaluation
    control = ctrl
  )

# 8. Results
## 5 best combinations using RMSE
show_best(res, metric = "rmse")


estimates <- collect_metrics(res)

## Predictions
collect_predictions(res)
# augment(res) %>% 
#   ggplot(aes(x=Total, y=.pred, color = Total)) +
#   geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
#   facet_wrap(~Total)


# 9. selection of best combination of hyperparameters 
best_params <- select_best(res, metric = "rmse")
best_params
autoplot(res)


# 10. Final workflow using selected hyperparameters
final_workflow <- wf %>%
  finalize_workflow(best_params)

# 11. fit the final model on the full training dataset and test it

final_model <- fit(final_workflow, data = train.forest) 
final_model 

final_plot <- extract_fit_engine(final_model)

png("Total_decision_tree_grid_search.png", width=1200, height = 800)
rpart.plot(final_plot,
           type = 4,
           cex = 1.5,
           extra = 101,
           box.palette = "Oranges")
dev.off()

test_predict <- predict(final_model, new_data = test.forest)

test_metrics <- test.forest %>%
  bind_cols(test_predict) %>%
  metrics(truth = Total, estimate = .pred)
test_metrics
```

```{r}
print(plot(varImp(bag02), top = 40)) # variables importance
# IllnessDuration, Age, Income_percapita, CGI, psychiatric, Density, 

# Partial dependence plots, stratum-wise
pdp_by_class <- function(model, var, train_data = train.forest.F) {
  grid_args <- if (var %in% area_vars) {
    list(pred.grid = setNames(data.frame(sort(unique(train_data[[var]]))), var))
  } else {
    list(grid.resolution = 40)
  }
  pdp_all <- map_dfr(c("low", "medium", "high"), function(cl) {
    do.call(pdp::partial, c(list(model, pred.var = var, prob = TRUE, which.class = cl), grid_args)) %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      mutate(class = cl)
  })

  p <- ggplot(pdp_all, aes(x = .data[[var]], y = yhat, color = class)) +
    geom_point(size = 4)
  if (is.numeric(pdp_all[[var]])) p <- p + geom_line(linetype = 3, linewidth = 1.5)

  p +
    labs(x = var, y = "Predicted probability") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 20), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
}

for (v in c("IllnessDuration", "Age", "Income_percapita", "CGI", "psychiatric", "Density")) {
  print(pdp_by_class(bag02, v))
}
```

## Bagging with randomForest (mtry = all predictors)

```{r}
# random forest
set.seed(42)
bag.complete = randomForest(Total_F ~ .,
                          data = train.forest.F.even,
                          mtry = ncol(train.forest.F.even)-1, # exclude dependant variable
                          importance = TRUE,
                          ntree = 1000)
bag.complete$err.rate # oob errors
plot(bag.complete$err.rate[,1], main = "OOB error", xlab = "n. of trees", type = "l")

plot(bag.complete$err.rate[,2], main = "Misclassification", xlab = "n. of trees", ylab = "prop. misclassification", type = "l", col = "red", ylim = c(0,.6))
lines(bag.complete$err.rate[,3], col = "darkgrey", type = "l")
lines(bag.complete$err.rate[,4], col = "lightgreen", type = "l")
legend("topright",
       pch = c(1,1,1),
       lwd = c(2,2,2),
       col = c("red","darkgrey","lightgreen"),
       legend = c("low", "medium", "high"),
       bty = "n",
       cex = .8)

which.min(bag.complete$err.rate[,1]) #find number of trees that produces the lowest OOB error

yhat.bag = predict(bag.complete, newdata = test.forest.F)
mean((as.character(yhat.bag) == as.character(test.forest.F$Total_F))) # accuracy

importance(bag.complete)
varImpPlot(bag.complete, main = "Importance plot") # variable importance plot

sample.tree = getTree(bag.complete, 200, labelVar = TRUE) # extract one tree from the forest
sample.tree
```

### Tuning

```{r}
set.seed(42)

model_tuned = tuneRF(x=train.forest.F.even[,-1], # define predictor variables
                     y=train.forest.F.even$Total_F, # define response variable
                     ntreeTry=500, # number of trees to build
                     mtryStart=4, # starting number of predictor variables to consider at each split
                     stepFactor=1.5, # factor to increase by until the out-of-bag estimated error stops improving by a certain amount
                     improve=0.01, # amount that the out-of-bag error needs to improve by to keep increasing the step factor
                     trace=FALSE,
                     plot=TRUE,
                     doBest = TRUE # gives directly the best model
               )
```

### Diagnostics and variable importance

```{r}
varImpPlot(rf.complete, main = "Importance plot - rf") # variable importance plot

yhat.bag.rf = predict(rf.complete, newdata = test.forest.F)
mean((as.character(yhat.bag.rf) == as.character(test.forest.F$Total_F))) # accuracy

# test against other data
confusionMatrix(data = yhat.bag.rf, reference = test.forest.F$Total_F)
# P-Value [Acc > NIR]: one-sided binomial test of the accuracy against the no-information rate; Mcnemar's Test: symmetry of the misclassifications

test.forest.F %>%
  bind_cols(.pred_class = yhat.bag.rf) %>%
  metrics(truth = Total_F, estimate = .pred_class)
```

### Ablation: random forest without territorial variables

```{r}
bal_acc = function(truth, pred) mean(sapply(levels(truth), function(l) mean(pred[truth == l] == l)), na.rm = TRUE)

set.seed(42)
rf.F.no.area = randomForest(Total_F ~ .,
                            data = dplyr::select(train.forest.F.even, -all_of(area_vars)),
                            mtry = round(sqrt(ncol(train.forest.F.even) - 1 - length(area_vars))),
                            ntree = 1000)
yhat.F.no.area = predict(rf.F.no.area, newdata = test.forest.F)

tibble(model = c("with territorial variables", "without territorial variables"),
       test_balanced_accuracy = c(bal_acc(test.forest.F$Total_F, yhat.bag.rf),
                                  bal_acc(test.forest.F$Total_F, yhat.F.no.area)))

set.seed(42)
boot.diff.F = replicate(2000, {
  i = sample(nrow(test.forest.F), replace = TRUE)
  bal_acc(test.forest.F$Total_F[i], yhat.bag.rf[i]) - bal_acc(test.forest.F$Total_F[i], yhat.F.no.area[i])
})
quantile(boot.diff.F, c(.025, .5, .975))
```

### Prediction (SHAP TEST: on a single individual)

```{r}
# SHAP test

#  explaining machine learning models with Shapley values. 
#  widely used approach from cooperative game theory that come with desirable properties.
explainer = DALEX::explain(model = rf.complete,
                            data = dplyr::select(train.forest.F.even, -Total_F),
                           y = train.forest.F.even$Total_F,
                     label = "Random Forest")

plot(model_performance(explainer = explainer))
plot(model_diagnostics(explainer = explainer))
explainer.test = DALEX::explain(model = rf.complete,
                                data = dplyr::select(test.forest.F, -Total_F),
                                y = test.forest.F$Total_F,
                                label = "Random Forest")

plot(model_parts(explainer = explainer.test,
            N = NULL)) # feature importance; use all observations
plot(model_parts(explainer = explainer.test,
            N = NULL,
            variable_groups = var_groups))

# SHAP values 
seven = dplyr::select(test.forest.F, -Total_F)[7,]
shap_perm = predict_parts(explainer, new_observation = seven,
                                        type = "shap", B = 10)
plot(shap_perm)
test.forest.F$Total_F[7]
predict(rf.complete, newdata = test.forest.F[7,])
# It includes the Shapley values and box plots summarizing the distributions of the variable-specific contributions for the selected random orderings.
# each permutation changes the order the variables are used in, and thus their relavite importance. Allows for an overall evaluation of variables importance

```

## Total_F: grid search

```{r cache = TRUE}

# for more annotations, see the corresponding chunk in TOTAL SCORE (Total: grid search)

# 1.
tree_char <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),  # cp
  tree_depth = tune(),       # maxdepth
  min_n = tune()             # minsplit
) %>%
  set_engine("rpart", model=TRUE) %>% 
  set_mode("classification") # qualitative variable

mlp_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(tree_char)
mlp_param

# 2.
recipe <- recipe(Total_F~., 
              data = train.forest.F2) %>%
  step_smotenc(Total_F, over_ratio = .8, neighbors = 5)

# 3.
ctrl<- control_grid(verbose = FALSE, save_pred = TRUE)

# 4.
wf2 <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(tree_char) %>%
  add_recipe(recipe)

# 5.
cost_complexity_values <- seq(0.01, 0.1, by = 0.01)
min_n_values <- seq(2, 10, by = 1)                          
tree_depth_values <- seq(3, 10, by = 1)  


grid <- expand.grid(
  cost_complexity = cost_complexity_values,
  min_n = min_n_values,
  tree_depth = tree_depth_values
)

# 6.
set.seed(42)
folds <- vfold_cv(train.forest.F2, v = 5, strata = Total_F)

# 7.
set.seed(42)
res <- wf2 %>%
  tune_grid(
    resamples = folds,
    grid = grid,
    metrics = metric_set(accuracy, roc_auc),
    control = ctrl
  )

# 8.
show_best(res, metric = "roc_auc")

# 9.
best_params <- select_best(res, metric = "roc_auc")
best_params


# 10.
final_workflow <- wf2 %>%
  finalize_workflow(best_params)


# 11.

final_model <- fit(final_workflow, data = train.forest.F2)
final_model

final_plot <- extract_fit_engine(final_model)

png("Total_F_decision_tree_grid_search.png", width=1200, height = 800)
rpart.plot(final_plot,
           type = 4,
           cex = 1.5,
           extra = 101)
dev.off()
```
